hook: In Hong Kong, millions of people live in apartment towers 30 or more stories high. In Houston, Texas, most homes are houses with their own yards. In Detroit, whole blocks that were packed with homes in 1950 are grassy fields in the 2020s. Why do cities house people so differently, and why does the same land fill up, empty out and fill up again?

prereq.q: Why are land values highest in the CBD?
options: It is the most accessible place, so users bid the most for it
It is farthest from the river
prereq.why: Bid-rent: the most accessible land draws the highest bids.

options: People per unit of land area
The share of people in cities

figure.caption: Residential density usually falls from downtown to the edge; infill adds homes on empty lots inside the built-up area.

chain.cause: Land near the center costs the most
chain.effect: builders put more homes on each lot, so residential density is highest near downtown

chain.cause: New technology (elevators, streetcars, then cars) changes how people move and build
chain.effect: cities grow up in some eras and spread out in others

chain.cause: Local governments pass zoning rules about what can be built where
chain.effect: some areas allow apartments and stores, others allow only single houses, which locks in a density pattern

chain.cause: An area ages, loses jobs or residents, and leaves empty lots
chain.effect: later investors and cities may fill the gaps with new buildings: infilling

ideas: Residential density is the number of homes (or people) on a given area of land. High-density housing means apartments; low-density housing means detached houses on large lots.

Housing reflects culture (courtyard homes for family privacy in old Fez, Morocco; single-family houses with yards in many US suburbs) and technology (elevators and steel frames made towers possible; cars made low-density suburbs possible).
Zoning is a set of local laws that says what kind of building and land use is allowed on each piece of land. It shapes density for decades.
Land goes through cycles of development: building, aging, decline and rebuilding. Infilling is building on vacant or underused lots inside an area that is already built up.

misconception.wrong: A city with a large population must have a high residential density.
misconception.right: Density compares homes or people with land area. A large city spread over a huge area, such as metro Atlanta, can have a low residential density, while a smaller city of apartment blocks can have a high one. Always ask "per how much land?"

summary: Housing and land use reflect culture, technology and the cycles of building and decline that every city goes through. Residential density is usually highest near the center and falls toward the edge. Zoning rules lock in density patterns, and infilling adds new buildings on empty lots inside the built-up area.
